comments.author: mindscanlabs
comments.body:
**An independent forecast of the final loss, with a law found from the data (no fixed form)**

I forecast the run's final `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss`: the last eval logged in the lineage at step 387,000 or later, as W&B records it (expected at 16K packing). I used only public W&B data, up to step 302,999 (snapshot of 2026-10-21, 22:58 UTC).

| forecast | data | value | 90 % interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | ladder + the hero's own evals | **1.979** | [1.965, 1.994] |
| B | ladder only | **1.935** | [1.915, 1.963] |

**Method in brief.** NAI, the symbolic-regression system I develop, finds a law L(C, fraction of training) from the table, with no form given: no floor and no power law are assumed. C is your lm_head-excluded compute.
- B is the ladder-only law at the hero's compute and the end of training.
- A adds the hero's post-swap 4K evals to the table and takes the level from its 16 evals at 16K.
- The intervals are NAI's forecast band, nominally 90 %.

B is 0.10 below the Aug 19 pre-registration from the same ladder, because the law NAI found has no fixed floor.

The formulas are sealed. Their SHA-256 digests and the scoring rules, fixed in advance: https://github.com/mindscanlabs/NAI-track-record/blob/main/forecasts/marin-535b.md

I'll post the formulas and the scored comparison after the run ends. Thanks for running this in the open: it makes a forecast like this possible.

comments.author: bethehand
comments.body: A measurement for anyone checking forecasts made while the evals packed at 4K (Marin's Aug 19 forecast of 2.039, and mine in #9977): the switch to 16K lowered the Paloma macro by about 0.031 on nearly the same weights. The `qk16k-a1-step252k` arm restored step 252,000 with the hero's post-switch settings (16K, `qk_mult` 1.48) and logged 2.0929 and 2.0926 at steps 252,049 and 252,099, against 2.1234 for the hero's 4K eval of that checkpoint, logged at step 251,999. With `qk_mult` left at 1.3 (`qk16k-a0-step252k`), the drop is about 0.028. The hero's own step from 254,999 to 257,999 looks smaller (0.024) because WikiText's dip at 254,999 lowered the last 4K eval; without WikiText it is 0.032 over those 3,000 steps. So a 4K-era forecast scored against the 16K final value, as in H1 and H4 of the forecast linked above, starts about 0.03 high from the packing change alone. The offset may also drift over the remaining 16K training, so if it's cheap, one 4K eval of the final checkpoint would let these forecasts be checked at the 4K packing they were built on. How I'll compare the forecasts at the end, fixed before phase 2, is in [this addendum](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/blob/phase2-plan-2026-10-22/addenda/2026-10-22_phase2_plan.md).

comments.author: bethehand
comments.body: A heads-up for the hero's planned 262K extension (#10618): with evals packed at the training context, Paloma's PTB and WikiText-103 val sets are each shorter than one 262,144-token sequence, so they yield no eval data ([`tokens // seq_len`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8577d258214dd0dcb992c04458ee4eb10496d4e5/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L93)). Their losses are then logged as 0.0 and the Paloma group macro skips them ([eval.py#L634-L636](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8577d258214dd0dcb992c04458ee4eb10496d4e5/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L634-L636)), so `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` silently becomes a 14-subset mean: at current values a jump of about +0.06 (about 3%), enough to trip `eval_regressed`. The top-level `macro_loss` instead averages the zeros in ([eval.py#L611](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8577d258214dd0dcb992c04458ee4eb10496d4e5/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L611)), about −0.14 on the hero's 23 tags. The 67B's 65K→262K switch, with the same tokenizer and Paloma files, shows both: from step 155,999 ([65K run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step141k)) to 156,000 ([262K run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep1_ctx4_bs256_seq262144_ctxext_step156k)), `eval/paloma/macro_loss` rose 2.1774 → 2.2150 while the other 14 subsets moved +0.0004, and `eval/macro_loss` fell 2.0260 → 1.8607 (2.0379 without the zeros). Either fix is small: mask zero-token tags in the top-level macro as the group macros already do, or keep all 16 subsets by setting `GrugEvalConfig.max_seq_len` (#9890) to 65,536 for the 262K phase.

comments.body:
**The forecast of 21 October, scored**

Follow-up to my forecast in this thread (2026-10-21). Target, as registered: the last `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` of the hero lineage at step 387,000 or later. That is **1.9602** at step 390,250 (`hero-ctx65k-step372k`), with all 16 Paloma subsets present.

| forecast | value | 90 % interval | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: ladder + the hero's own evals | 1.979 | [1.965, 1.994] | 0.019 |
| B: ladder only | 1.935 | [1.915, 1.963] | 0.025 |
| line through the hero's 16K evals (my baseline) | 1.970 | | 0.009 |
| Aug 19 pre-registration | 2.039 | | 0.079 |

Hypotheses fixed in advance:
- A closer than 2.039: yes.
- B closer than 2.039: yes.
- The final value inside A's interval: no, below it by 0.0045.
- A closer than the straight line: no.

The final value is inside B's interval.

**Packing.** 2.039 and B were built on 4K-packed evals, so the comparison above favours them against a training-length eval. Thanks to the 4K re-evaluation (`hero-ctx-evals-4k`), the offset at the last re-evaluated checkpoint is 1.9817 (4K, step 390,000) minus 1.9590 (the run's eval, step 389,999) = 0.0227. That is smaller than the 0.031 measured at step 252K. Against 1.9602 + 0.0227 = 1.983, B is off by 0.048 and 2.039 by 0.056. So both forecasts are still closer after the correction.

The formulas are unsealed now and match the SHA-256 digests posted before the outcome, as does the registration's manifest: https://github.com/mindscanlabs/NAI-track-record/blob/main/forecasts/marin-535b.md

These forecasts were made with version 19 of NAI.
NAI is now at version 25, and I would be glad to join your next experiment with it.

Thanks for logging, re-evaluating and discussing all of this in the open, and to @bethehand for the packing measurements. They made a clean prospective test possible.

Training loss over the last 1,000 steps averaged 0.965, at 65K context. MFU ended near 33%. The 4K row re-evaluates the last 6K checkpoint; the 65K row is the run's own final eval.

**Training loss.** Every step is plotted, against tokens trained. The dashed lines mark the switch to near-dropless EP (ragged all-to-all), the two datamix changes, and the 4K → 16K and 16K → 65K context extensions.
![training loss](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_train_loss.png)

**Against the scaling ladder**, by run progress. At 80% the ladder moved to its phase-2 mix and its loss rose; the hero moved to a different phase-2 mix and its loss fell. The 27.7B rung crashed at 81% on a hardware failure and was not resumed.
![hero against the scaling ladder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_vs_ladder_train_loss.png)

**Forecast and actual, every eval at 4K context.** The forecast is the per-5% ladder fit posted earlier in this issue. The hero tracks it to about 65%, then pulls ahead after extending to 16K and then 65K context with an improved datamix. From the 16K switch on, the hero points are the 4K re-evaluations of every 6K checkpoint (W&B `hero-evals-at-4k`).
![forecast and actual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_evals_vs_forecast.png)

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Weight merging the final hero checkpoints: −0.003 loss at 65K, saved as a resumable checkpoint**

Averaging the final 65K-phase checkpoints lowers loss by about 0.003 on every eval. On the ladder law L = 1.5 + 84.8·C^−0.09 that's worth roughly 7% more training compute, for free.

**Checkpoint:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251`

- **Weights:** an equal-weight average of 11 checkpoints: 385,500–390,000 every 500 steps, plus the final 390,251. Each weight tensor is rescaled to stay on the hyperball (details below).
- **Training state:** step 390,251, with that checkpoint's full optimizer state and QB betas. It has the hero's checkpoint layout, so it resumes directly with `initialize_from` or loads weights-only for evals and export.
- **`metadata.json`** records the sources, the weights, the merge space and where the training state came from.

All evals are dropless at 65,536 context with `qk_mult` 1.66. Each row is the change versus step 390,000.

| Merge | Clean Paloma | Uncheatable | All evals |
|---|---|---|---|
| step 390,000 (baseline) | 1.7515 | 1.4786 | 1.6953 |
| step 390,251 (final) | −0.0001 | −0.0003 | ±0.0000 |
| average of last 2 | −0.0012 | −0.0011 | −0.0013 |
| average of last 4 | −0.0020 | −0.0020 | −0.0021 |
| EMA, 0.5 per 500 steps (10 ckpts) | −0.0020 | −0.0019 | −0.0021 |
| EMA, 0.8 per 500 steps (10 ckpts) | −0.0028 | −0.0029 | −0.0029 |
| average of 10 (385,500–390,000) | −0.0028 | −0.0031 | −0.0030 |
| average of 10, hyperball | −0.0028 | −0.0031 | −0.0029 |
| **average of 11, hyperball (saved)** | **−0.0030** | **−0.0033** | **−0.0032** |

- **What matters:** how many checkpoints go in, and how evenly they're weighted. The wider and flatter the average, the bigger the gain, and it hadn't levelled off at 11.
- **Hyperball rescaling changes nothing:** the plain average already sits at 0.9995 of the sphere radius.
- **Step-to-step noise is small:** one more stretch of training (390,000 → 390,251) moves the loss by at most 0.0003, an order of magnitude less than the merge.
- **Every eval set improves,** all 23 of them.

**Process**

1. **Choosing eval sets:** the 4K re-evals of the 16K and 65K checkpoints showed which sets don't fall smoothly from step to step. "Clean Paloma" leaves out PTB (contaminated reads), WikiText-103, TwitterAAE and Gab, whose loss rose 7–12 times across those 23 checkpoints. It averages the other 12 sets. "Uncheatable" averages all 7 of its sets.
2. **Merging:** sources load one at a time into a float32 running sum of the fp32 weights. The hero keeps no separate master copy, so these are the master weights.
3. **Hyperball mode:** after averaging, each MuonH/AdamH tensor is rescaled to its sources' mean norm, over the same axes the optimizer holds fixed:
   - 2-D weights: the whole matrix is one ball.
   - Stacked weights: one ball per layer.
   - Routed experts: each layer's whole bank of all 384 experts is one ball (`ALL_EXPERTS`).

   Adam-trained leaves (embeddings, router, norm gains, attention gate) are plain averages.
4. **Saving:** the merged weights are combined with 390,251's step, optimizer state and QB betas, using a template built from the hero's own optimizer config. Before launching, I checked that template against the 390,251 manifest: all 56 optimizer-state arrays and 36 parameter arrays match in shape and dtype.
5. **Verification:** the job reloaded the saved checkpoint and checked the weights bit for bit and the optimizer state by per-leaf checksums. The eval numbers above for the saved row come from that reloaded copy.

Each variant ran as one job on one rack at production priority, logged to W&B in `marin_moe` as `hero-merge-*` (the saved one is `hero-merge-hb-avg11-save`).

**Code:** branch [`larry/hero-ckpt-merge-eval`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/larry/hero-ckpt-merge-eval) at [`dff14a5`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/dff14a54199eaf97a3719d0b6d64a99fb044d47f). The work is in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_checkpoint_eval.py`, using `--merge-source PATH WEIGHT` (repeatable), `--merge-space hyperball` and `--save-merged OUT STATE_FROM`; the CPU tests are in `test_checkpoint_eval.py`. The saved checkpoint was made with:

```
python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_checkpoint_eval --run-id hero-merge-hb-avg11-save \
  --merge-source <ckpts>/step-385500 1 ... --merge-source <ckpts>/step-390000 1 --merge-source <ckpts>/step-390251 1 \
  --merge-qk-mult 1.66 --merge-space hyperball \
  --save-merged s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251 <ckpts>/step-390251 \
  --seq-len 65536 --version dev --run
```

where `<ckpts>` = `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-step372k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints`.

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 The 262K extension is decided: two recipes in sequence, from [the merged checkpoint](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6676769570), 3,240 steps or 149.5B tokens each, to step 393491. The learning rate moves linearly from 5% to 1% of peak. First, Global 1.84 (`qk_mult` 1.66, long scale 1.108), from main at `e0bc917ee5`. Second, log floor 65536 squared, from a branch that merges only if it wins.

Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks did not separate the recipes on held-out text: clean macro at 262K spans 0.0004, against jitter of 0.0002 to 0.0007. The merged start's gain on clean macro fell from about 0.003 to 0.0017 in 100 steps, on one seed. Global 1.84 ran in no arm, no rehearsal ran, and no arm was repeated. An arm that held the router bias fixed was not adopted, so the bias keeps updating each step.

Changes to what you may rely on: a checkpoint from the second finalist cannot be exported or served until log-scaling support lands, SFT and RL loading of the merged checkpoint is untested, and at 262K `ptb` and `wikitext_103` write no online eval value. Offline evals still score them.

Results and full evidence: [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37) and its [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2307cd320fb832c022284d6df07858db3b89d5f/logbooks/37-hero-262k/notebook.md). Tracking: #11056.

issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
issues.body:
Add a Grafana alert for sustained unused B200 cluster capacity. The current Grafana provisioning has GPU utilization data and operational alerts, but no alert that surfaces a B200 cluster sitting idle while its GPUs are available. Start from the existing GPU utilization signal in `infra/grafana/src/accelerator_observability.py` and the provisioned rules in `infra/grafana/provisioning/alerting/rules.yaml`.

Done when:
- A provisioned rule detects sustained low utilization of available B200 GPUs, with a documented threshold and evaluation window that avoid firing on brief gaps between workloads.
- The alert identifies the affected cluster and reports the observed utilization and available capacity, with a link to the relevant Grafana view.
- The rule routes a notification to the appropriate operations contact point. Missing telemetry is distinguishable from genuine idleness.
- Tests cover a sustained idle cluster, an active cluster, and missing telemetry.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
`LocalMachineFactory()` fails on some `cw-rno2a` workers with `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'pidfd_open'`. The task's interpreter on those workers is a uv-cached CPython 3.12.12 (`/uv/cache/python/cpython-3.12.12-linux-x86_64-gnu`), whose `os` module has no `pidfd_open`. Shellbox calls it when it probes bubblewrap (`lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py:572`) and again at `machine.py:386`. Workers of the same job image that resolved CPython 3.12.16 have `os.pidfd_open` and work. `.python-version` pins only `3.12`, so the interpreter depends on what the node has cached.

The error is permanent. A Zephyr pipeline whose workers build a `LocalMachineFactory` fails as a whole: 3 of 4 workers of `/rav/agentic-drafts-ramp-4` hit it on 2026-11-06, and the job failed before any work ran.

```
File "/app/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py", line 1118, in __init__
    self.bwrap = _working_bwrap(_bwrap_candidates(bwrap), system_directories)
File "/app/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py", line 311, in _working_bwrap
    error = _prepare_sandbox(candidate, system_directories)
File "/app/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py", line 572, in _allocate_keeper
    self._keeper_pidfd = os.pidfd_open(self._keeper.pid)
AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'pidfd_open'
```

Reproduce:
1. Submit an Iris job on `cw-rno2a` with `--container-profile container_profile_privileged` whose task runs `python -c "from shellbox.backends.local.machine import LocalMachineFactory; LocalMachineFactory()"`.
2. On a node whose uv cache resolves `3.12` to CPython 3.12.12, the call raises the error above. On a 3.12.16 worker of the same image, `python -c "import os, sys; print(sys.version, hasattr(os, 'pidfd_open'))"` prints `True`; I have not run it on a 3.12.12 worker.

Expected: every worker resolves an interpreter that has `os.pidfd_open`, or `LocalMachineFactory` reports `SandboxUnavailable` with the reason. Passing `-e UV_PYTHON 3.12.16` to the job works around it.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

Iris serializes the submitter's Python as major.minor and passes that to `uv sync --python`, so workers may choose different cached 3.12 patch builds. Shellbox requires `os.pidfd_open` to pin the keeper and init processes, but checks neither that API nor `signal.pidfd_send_signal` before probing bubblewrap. The uv-managed 3.12.13 interpreter in this checkout also lacks both APIs.

Relevant code: [Iris version selection](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L800), [uv setup command](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/setup_scripts.py#L80), [Shellbox keeper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L572), [repository Python pin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.python-version).

**Proposed Fix**

Pin this repository to the reported working 3.12.16 build, pass the submitter's exact patch version to Iris task setup, and have Shellbox raise `SandboxUnavailable` before starting a probe when its interpreter lacks either required pidfd API. This preserves the pidfd-based process identity and cleanup behavior.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

The factory's bubblewrap probe calls `os.pidfd_open` while starting its keeper ([machine.py:572](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5e8a9cfe9d9d50b79fd03e4ed0ed0087edf627d/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L572)); it calls the same API when pinning init ([machine.py:386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5e8a9cfe9d9d50b79fd03e4ed0ed0087edf627d/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L386)). The local uv-managed CPython 3.12.13 lacks both `os.pidfd_open` and `signal.pidfd_send_signal`. Iris generates `uv sync --python 3.12` from the submitter's minor version ([types.py:800](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5e8a9cfe9d9d50b79fd03e4ed0ed0087edf627d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L800)), so a patch-level `.python-version` pin alone would not determine the task interpreter.

**Proposed Fix**

Pin this checkout to CPython 3.12.15, make Iris's default 3.12 worker setup request at least that patch release, and have `LocalMachineFactory` raise `SandboxUnavailable` with the missing pidfd capability before probing bubblewrap. I installed uv's CPython 3.12.15 locally and confirmed it has both pidfd APIs. This session's uv 0.13.5 catalog does not yet list 3.12.16.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 Fix proposed in #11017: pin Marin to the verified uv CPython 3.12.15 build, make Iris select it for all Python 3.12 task setups, and raise `SandboxUnavailable` when Shellbox lacks a required pidfd API. The nearby Iris and Shellbox tests pass (21 cases); the advisory lint review found no issues. The production-run incident and workaround are recorded in [Echo](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/937).

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 `-e UV_PYTHON 3.12.16` does not work around this. Iris builds the task venv with `uv sync --python 3.12` (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py:800` takes only the client's major and minor version), and that flag overrides `UV_PYTHON`. uv prefers managed interpreters, so a node whose `/uv/cache` holds a managed CPython 3.12.12 gets it.

`-e UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE only-system` does work around it. uv then uses the image's own Python, `/usr/local` 3.12.16, which has `os.pidfd_open`. Zephyr child jobs inherit the variable. All 4 workers of `/rav/agentic-drafts-ramp-4c` resolved `/usr/local` 3.12.16, and none raised the error.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Why pods differ.** I compared per-task setup lines and pidfd errors in the `marin` Finelog hub's `log` namespace for `cw-rno2a`, 2026-11-06 03:00–04:00 UTC.

| Run | Worker interpreters selected by uv | Workers logging `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'pidfd_open'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agentic-drafts-ramp-4` | worker 0: 3.12.14; workers 1–3: 3.12.12 | 1–3 |
| `agentic-drafts-ramp-4b` | worker 0: system 3.12.16; workers 1–2: 3.12.14; worker 3: 3.12.12 | 3 |
| `agentic-drafts-ramp-4c` (`UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system`) | all four: `/usr/local/bin/python3.12` 3.12.16 | none as of 04:35 UTC; job running |

I also inspected live `ramp-4c` pods. Their `/uv/cache` volume is a node-local `hostPath` at `/mnt/local/iris-cache/uv-cache`, so different nodes retain different Python builds. On one live node, the cached 3.12.12 binary lacks both `os.pidfd_open` and `signal.pidfd_send_signal`, while `/usr/local/bin/python` 3.12.16 has both in the same pod and kernel. An isolated `uv python find 3.12` probe chose cached 3.12.12 by default and `/usr/local/bin/python3.12` with `only-system`. A cached 3.12.14 binary on another node has both APIs.

The per-node cache and uv interpreter selection explain the pod-to-pod behavior. The evidence rules out the Linux kernel alone as the cause: two interpreters in one live pod differ in API availability. The exact historical pod images were not retained for comparison.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 ([open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1), revision adc0078a) calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with *real reasoning*, in this case supplied by GLM 5.3. Also, tool replay needed to be doubled to keep BFCL scores. 
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Report (PDF):** [snowball-identity.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf) (15 pages, 2026-11-04). One paper covers the context-distillation phase and the identity-data SFT arms, with the three experiment diagrams. It replaces the two earlier PDFs.
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

**Eval policy results (updated 2026-11-06):** the full benchmark tables for this experiment's candidates are in [this comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6665512022) and are updated in place after each reviewed delta.

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702
- On-policy distillation (paused after 20 steps; results in #10732): #10730, #10731, #10732

## Status

- **Path B (identity data) is the active track.** A13 is the lead candidate; A3 is the fallback. Both, plus A8a, are archived in public open-athena HF repos (made public 2026-11-03). Public artifacts: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30), [A8a](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30), [A11](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A11-2026.10.30/tree/6834175e6d4a021039fa04d3c374ccfd6fbdeb51), and A13's exact training inputs ([dataset @05d9bba9](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Identity-PathB-A13-Inputs-2026.10.30/tree/05d9bba9d6227aa1644f92c3f88476f42ff906fe)), from which the packed training file rebuilds byte for byte (SHA256 f860030d).
- **Still running:** Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime needed environment snapshots and has a grader bug, so only the agentic part is being piloted.
- **Earlier context-distillation runs** (above) did not meet the ship lines. The earlier "ship the default system prompt" recommendation is withdrawn: the goal is for the model itself to know it is not ChatGPT.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

Iris job: `/benfeuer/cd16-native60-r2-20261026`. The generation task completed successfully and its outputs were retrieved before temporary-storage expiry.

The OPD pools are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer targets, and overlap each other. Both repositories use automatic gated access. They are sources to inspect for name-first and varied false-premise prompts; I have not counted those subsets here. Keep evaluation rows separate, and avoid importing the SFT corpus wholesale: #10491 documents its identity overgeneralization and fiction regressions.

Still missing from our results are this panel with **your default system prompt** and evaluations of **the new OPD and tool-data candidates**. Those require new inference. The existing 60 questions are a development panel that guided earlier data expansion, so reuse supports continuity rather than an untouched generalization claim.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **A13** | **35 / 32 / 0** | **29 / 30 / 1** | **3** | **0 / 0** |
| A9 | 32 / 40 / 1 | 28 / 39 / 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| A10 | 26 / 32 / 9 | 29 / 24 / 5 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| A11 | 31 / 37 / 2 | 27 / 39 / 1 | 16 | 1 / 1 |
| A12 | 30 / 33 / 1 | 31 / 35 / 3 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| M25 | 32 / 45 / 0 | 29 / 33 / 0 | 18 | 0 / 0 |
| M49 | 30 / 40 / 0 | 29 / 32 / 0 | 13 | 0 / 0 |
| M51 | 33 / 31 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

Shared notes:

- † identifies only cell-specific qualifications below. Shared benchmark conventions do not create markers. No clean capability inference is made from a DIAG cell; all scores and intervals remain pinned measurements.
- These 26 benchmarks are the in-distribution development panel, not held-out/OOD evaluation. Intervals are admitted scored-sample SEM/√0.9, not missingness-bias protection. Missing outcomes remain NULL; planned-outcome bounds are separate non-CI sensitivity ranges.
- AIME24 and Olympiad: 30 prompts × 10 scored trials. GPQA: 198 prompts × 3 scored trials. Trial intervals are not prompt-cluster CIs or repeat-to-repeat stderr. A missing planned count is reported as unavailable, never as an unset denominator.
- PIQA uses raw acc; acc_norm and its coverage.n_correct numerator are separate. Current Crux is combined input+output, 1600 cases; historical tracker Crux is output-only, a different code version. TruthfulQA/MRCR use continuous sample SEM, not binary success fractions.
- HumanEval+/MBPP+ use the native accuracy-to-pass@1 alias and share the code-extractor qualification. v0.1 can emit real reasoning in thinking-off code benchmarks. Deterministic 30-sample rates are descriptive, not population estimates; “many” means ≥10/30 changed parses. The 30-sample sweep does not regrade or alter pinned primary grades. The separately labelled secondary reports independently regraded outputs.
- Thinking-off counts use the matched fresh v0.1 reference even where its row is not displayed. TriviaQA is excluded from campaign pairwise analysis. Its pinned primary values stay primary; think-stripped secondary measurements are separately labelled as a different extraction, with the primary unchanged. Matched v0.1 reference: 57.0% [56.2,57.7].
- NUPA uses post-#10733/#10876 scoring. historical cohort-adjusted scalars are not new matched scores.

comments.body:
## Plain-language summary of the identity SFT work

The full eval policy has now run on the finished arms, so this is a recap of the whole thread for readers who did not follow it day by day. Numbers and links are in the body and the result tables above.

**Starting point.** Snowball v0.1 ([open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1)) calls itself ChatGPT (thinking on) or Nemotron (thinking off) when there is no system prompt. With an identity system prompt it mostly answers as Marin, but not reliably (blind Panel-60: name 26/60, creator 40/60, four foreign claims).

**What did not work before this thread.**
- An identity SFT on v0.1 (v0.1.1) learned the identity but lost capability broadly (MMLU-Pro -21, HumanEval+ -29, GSM8K -28). Transferring that knowledge into v0.1 with OPD was shelved after behavioural validation ([OPD follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491#issuecomment-6371754500)).
- Interpretability work, task-vector steering and model merging did not give a usable model ([Discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1550024637927268392/1567700162506137772)).
- Context distillation (v0.1 with the system prompt as teacher, v0.1 as student, 16 updates, replay added) learned the creator (38/52) but barely the name (2-6/52) and collapsed tool calling (BFCL 27.6% to 7.3%). In hindsight this is the same failure the later ablations isolated: identity rows rendered with thinking on teach the model to answer and stop.

**What this thread did.** Short SFTs from v0.1 (36 updates, lr 2e-6, 8 x 8,192 packed tokens) on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data), deduplicated and capped per answer type; about 6,000 rows, one in seven of the set), mixed with replay of v0.1's own answers to fresh maths, code, chat and tool-calling prompts. Identity is about 10% of the supervised tokens, replay 90%. Will's own 2026-10-05 SFT had shown the data works with thinking off (name 30/52) but not on (14/52, 30 foreign claims in 122 prompts).

**What the ablations found.**
- Identity rows rendered with thinking on are the problem. With an empty think span, or with all of them carrying generated reasoning, BFCL falls to about 15%. Rendered with thinking off only (A3), tool calling is the best of any arm (31.1%), but the model then invents a "system message" in its reasoning on 17/52 prompts.
- A small thinking-on share is tolerable. A8a keeps 179 identity rows (3% of identity rows) with short GLM-written rationales that pass a QC filter, the rest thinking off: BFCL 26.2%, -1.5 [-4.9, +1.5] vs v0.1. At 9% (A8b) BFCL drops to 17%.
- A13 is A8a with the thinking-on tool-calling replay rows duplicated, at the same compute. BFCL 28.3%, +0.7 [-3.4, +4.4]; the difference from A8a is inside the five-run noise.
- More training (72 updates), less (18), a small Tulu-style identity set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and self-distilling the reasoning from v0.1 did not help.

**Where it stands.** A13 is the lead and A3 the fallback. A13 never claims another lab with thinking on (v0.1: 46/52) and names itself on 35/52. It is not a clean win: GSM8K -1.1 [-1.9, -0.3], Terminal-Bench Lite 12.7 vs 22.5, SOTOPIA-hard 61.9 vs 65.9, and single-run agentic cells favour A3 (Terminal-Bench 2 10.6 vs 6.4, BixBench 11.7 vs 6.8). 22 of 26 benchmarks overlap v0.1. Weights: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30). These are research checkpoints; the release call is open.

> *What this thread did.* Short SFTs from v0.1 (36 updates, lr 2e-6, 8 x
> 8,192 packed tokens) on Will Held's identity data (
> marin-community/identity-data
> <https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__huggingface.co_datasets_marin-2Dcommunity_identity-2Ddata&d=DwMFaQ&c=slrrB7dE8n7gBJbeO0g-IQ&r=cRVZDAsVf8YMy7ncQBvRsw&m=w8fvlI8P_TjZX1y8zZFEjHoSRMBG8aCugpFvq-W4k81QgHMgtL1yYKIPygr5rhWA&s=ful1hOk1ScAsbxryGjrGMWI8BOg16LMiinhOnukvoGQ&e=>,
> deduplicated and capped per answer type; about 6,000 rows, one in seven of
> the set), mixed with replay of v0.1's own answers to fresh maths, code,
> chat and tool-calling prompts. Identity is about 10% of the supervised
> tokens, replay 90%. Will's own 2026-10-05 SFT had shown the data works with
> thinking off (name 30/52) but not on (14/52, 30 foreign claims in 122
> prompts).
>
> *What the ablations found.*
>
>    - Identity rows rendered with thinking on are the problem. With an
>    empty think span, or with all of them carrying generated reasoning, BFCL
>    falls to about 15%. Rendered with thinking off only (A3), tool calling is
>    the best of any arm (31.1%), but the model then invents a "system message"
>    in its reasoning on 17/52 prompts.
>    - A small thinking-on share is tolerable. A8a keeps 179 identity rows
>    (3% of identity rows) with short GLM-written rationales that pass a QC
>    filter, the rest thinking off: BFCL 26.2%, -1.5 [-4.9, +1.5] vs v0.1. At 9%
>    (A8b) BFCL drops to 17%.
>    - A13 is A8a with the thinking-on tool-calling replay rows duplicated,
>    at the same compute. BFCL 28.3%, +0.7 [-3.4, +4.4]; the difference from A8a
>    is inside the five-run noise.
>    - More training (72 updates), less (18), a small Tulu-style identity
>    set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and self-distilling the reasoning from
>    v0.1 did not help.
>
> *Where it stands.* A13 is the lead and A3 the fallback. A13 never claims
> another lab with thinking on (v0.1: 46/52) and names itself on 35/52. It is
> not a clean win: GSM8K -1.1 [-1.9, -0.3], Terminal-Bench Lite 12.7 vs 22.5,
> SOTOPIA-hard 61.9 vs 65.9, and single-run agentic cells favour A3
> (Terminal-Bench 2 10.6 vs 6.4, BixBench 11.7 vs 6.8). 22 of 26 benchmarks
> overlap v0.1. Weights: A13
> <https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__huggingface.co_open-2Dathena_Snowball-2D67B-2DA2B-2DIdentity-2DPathB-2DA13-2D2026.10.30&d=DwMFaQ&c=slrrB7dE8n7gBJbeO0g-IQ&r=cRVZDAsVf8YMy7ncQBvRsw&m=w8fvlI8P_TjZX1y8zZFEjHoSRMBG8aCugpFvq-W4k81QgHMgtL1yYKIPygr5rhWA&s=QXQkphj34hWQoKt1IkUQdUeDU8apAggiLoJdTEnf4qw&e=>,

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
This issue tracks extending the hero run ([#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435)) from 65K to 262,144-token context. Run status lives in [#8506](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8506). The recipe research lives in [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37). The 65K switch was [#10821](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10821) and [#10820](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10820).

## Plan

Train two recipes one after the other from step 390251 to step 393491, 3,240 steps or 149.5B tokens each, then compare them. Each finalist runs on 11 racks with context parallelism 4 and expert parallelism 16 (CP4 × EP16) and 16 sequences per rack, so 176 in all, and takes about 27 h at 29.9 s/step with saves (estimate).

Parent: `hero-ctx65k-step372k`, final checkpoint `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-step372k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-390251`. The merged start is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251`, an equal-weight hyperball average of the last 11 permanent checkpoints (details on [#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6676769570)).

## Status

First finalist `hero-lce-global184-step390k` is launching from main at `e0bc917ee5`, about 21:40 UTC on 2026-11-06. Go or no-go follows on #8506.

Second finalist `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k` launches after it, at `0454bdd609` on the branch of draft [#11044](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11044), when the first ends.

Both appear in the W&B report, [Hero 262K finalists](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Hero-262K-finalists--VmlldzoxODI2NjQ1Nw==).

## Configuration

| Field | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| First finalist | Global 1.84: `qk_mult` 1.66, long scale 1.108 | Merged, [#11041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11041) |
| Second finalist | Log floor 65536, slope 0.1, power 2, global layers | Branch; merges only if it wins, at the comparison on Monday 2026-11-09 |
| Start | Merged checkpoint at step 390251 | Merged, #11041 |
| Loader queue | 64 batches, down from 512 | Merged, #11041 |
| Run length | 3,240 steps, stop step 393491, 149.5B tokens | Merged, #11041 |
| Learning rate | Linear from 5% to 1% of peak over the 3,240 steps | Merged; the #11041 review approved the PR that states it |
| Router bias | Updates each step, as before | A frozen-bias arm was not adopted |
| Evals | In-loop at 262K every 500 steps, with a final eval at the stop | Padded windows and multi-length evals are not in this launch |
| Checkpoints | Seven permanent, about 30 TB per finalist (inferred) | Merged, #11041 |
| Data | Documents above 65,536 tokens at 4× sampling weight, 43.9% of tokens | [#10980](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10980), merged |
| Capacity factor | 1.5 | Unchanged |

The earlier switches set `qk_mult` from 1.3 × (1 + 0.1 ln(N/4096)) on all layers: 1.48 at 16K and 1.66 at 65K. Global 1.84 takes the value that rule gives at 262K and applies it to global layers only. No training arm ran it. It lies between Keep 1.66 and Global 1.88, which were trained.

## Evidence

Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks, on the launch data mix, from step 390251: six recipes from the merged checkpoint and Keep 1.66 (`qk_mult` unchanged) from the raw one. Each arm is one seed. "Global X" means global layers at X and other layers at 1.66. Clean macro is the mean loss over 19 held-out subsets. MRCR is the paired retrieval eval from [#8701](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8701); full NLL is its loss with the whole document in context, and recovery is the share of the evidence's benefit that survives in a long document. The logbook defines these fully. The [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2307cd320fb832c022284d6df07858db3b89d5f/logbooks/37-hero-262k/notebook.md) has full tables, commands, commits and negative results. W&B: `hero-lce11*` and `hero-mrcr-lce11*` in [`marin_moe`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe).

- Held-out text does not separate the merged recipes. Clean macro at 262K spans 0.0004 (1.6451 to 1.6455), against checkpoint jitter of 0.0002 to 0.0007.
- Retrieval (MRCR full NLL) differences survive correction across documents only, since no arm was repeated. The second finalist is 0.0017 below Keep 1.66 (corrected p 0.002) and 0.0014 below Global 1.88 (corrected p 0.001). Global 1.88 is not separated from Keep 1.66 (corrected p 1.00).
- Recovery does not separate the arms from Keep 1.66 after correction. It is 0.982 to 0.984 everywhere.
- The merged start was 0.0017 lower on clean macro than raw after 100 steps, down from about 0.003, on one seed. It may not last the run. Retrieval did not change.
- Raising the scale produces gradient spikes in the first two steps: 6.31 for Global 1.88 and 19.65 for the second finalist, against 0.62 for Keep 1.66. Gradients are clipped at 1.0. Whether this matters past 100 steps is not known.
- Holding the router bias at the merged checkpoint's value, in one more 100-step arm against the merged Global 1.88 arm, was not adopted. The rule, fixed before submission, needed clean macro better by more than 0.0007, and the change was 0.00015. Drops were 1.05x, under the 2x reject line. Full NLL was 0.0010 lower [-0.0015, -0.0006]. That arm's grad norm reached 83.56 on one step, against 0.19 in the control. The cause is unexplained, and one run cannot show whether freezing caused it.
- Memory: the train loader's 512-batch queue lives in device memory, and growth largely ends when it first wraps. One batch leaves per step, so queue 64 wraps every 64 steps. At queue 64 the tightest of 704 devices had 3.86 GiB free, against 2.08 GiB at 512, in runs that differ in recipe and start. On one rack at queue 64, a slow remainder of growth reached zero by the fourth wrap. Trimming the memory pool did not stop growth.

## Not tested

1. Global 1.84 in training. No rehearsal ran, so this launch is the first GPU training run of its recipe and of the code at `e0bc917ee5`.
2. Any 11-rack run past 100 steps, so also the queue-64 memory trend at 11 racks past its first wrap.
3. The learning-rate schedule at this length. The arms ran the same 5% start on a 4,335-step schedule, so this run's rate falls about 34% faster per step.
4. The 11-rack stop path. `HERO_SCHEDULE_EXTENSION` ([#10917](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10917), merged) was tested on one rack, on an earlier deploy head.
5. SFT and RL loading of the merged checkpoint, for any recipe.
6. Export of the second finalist. Hero exports refuse log scaling until serving support lands, so that checkpoint cannot be served yet. [#10986](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10986) (open) adds the slope and power fields.
7. Repeats. No arm has a second seed, so training noise at 11 racks is unmeasured.
8. Code on the launch commit that no arm ran. This includes #10556, which skips short-convolution weight gradients for frozen weights. Hero weights are not frozen, and reading the source and a CPU check with stand-in kernels show no effect. We did not check compiled GB200 code. It also includes [#11054](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11054), which changes only how eval macros are computed on the host after the eval loop.

## Reading the first evals

Training evals drop each corpus's final partial window, so `ptb` and `wikitext_103` have no window at 262K and write no online value. [#10711](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10711), which adds padded windows and multi-length evals, is not in this launch. Offline evals pad instead, so they still score both subsets.

- `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` excludes both subsets, which moves the parent's 1.960 to 2.043 at step 390251 with no change in the model.
- The `eval_regressed` alert compares each eval with the previous two, so it should fire on the child's first two evals for that reason, the first near step 390500 and about 2 h in. It is expected, and it does not show a regression. No run has shown it yet.
- `eval_dropless/macro_loss` now excludes both subsets too (#11054), and read 1.85 on the first eval, at W&B step 390499. The 100-step arms averaged them in as zeros and read about 1.78, so that series is not comparable with theirs.
- In-loop and offline levels differ. In the arms, the in-loop eval read 0.0040 above the offline eval on the 12 clean Paloma subsets. The finalist comparison uses offline evals.

The `throughput_low` alert has a floor of 2.0M tokens per second, and this run trains at about 1.58M, so it should also fire for as long as the floor stands. It does not affect training.

## Gates

These values are confirmed.

| When | Check | Expected | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restore | One coordinator; restored step 390251 from the merged path; optimizer counts match | | Any mismatch |
| First steps | Train cross-entropy; step time; drop fraction; learning rate | Cross-entropy below 1.25; about 29 s/step; near the arms' 2.9e-4; 5% of peak | Cross-entropy at or above 1.25 |
| First hour | Optimizer, learning-rate and parameter-norm graphs, read by eye | No step or jump | Reviewer judgment |
| About 33 min into training | Largest device memory in use after the first queue wrap | Near 179.4 GiB | Above 180 GiB means queue 64 did not land |
| After the first eval and each restart | Largest device memory in use, of 184.30 GiB | 180.44 GiB; pass up to 180.75 | Above 182.25 GiB |

There is no matched control: the parent ended at step 390251. Compare with the parent's last steps and the 11-rack arms at matching steps.

## Checklist

### A. Decisions

- [x] **A1** Start from the merged checkpoint.
- [x] **A2** Finalists and their order.
- [x] **A3** Loader queue 64.
- [x] **A4** Learning-rate schedule.
- [x] **A5** Frozen router bias: not adopted.
- [ ] **A6** Gates, and go or no-go for the second finalist.

### B. Code

- [x] **B1** [#10917](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10917) stop step, merged as `7903eda6d1`.
- [x] **B2** Deploy PR for the first finalist, [#11041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11041), merged as `cac11d381a`: `HERO_MODEL`, schedule extension, `HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES`, `HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL`, `current_run.py`, `trigger_hero.sh`.
- [x] **B3** [#11054](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11054) eval macros, merged as `e0bc917ee5`, the launch commit.
- [ ] **B4** Second finalist: [#11044](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11044), a branch carrying [#10986](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10986), merged only if it wins.
- [ ] **B5** Serving support for log scaling, before SFT or RL uses the second finalist.

### C. Tests

- [x] **C1** Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks, and one frozen-bias arm.
- [x] **C2** Stop path on one rack, on an earlier deploy head (`d0d4e15f45`).
- [ ] **C3** SFT and RL load test of the merged checkpoint. Not required for this launch; still to do.

### D. Launch, for each finalist

- [ ] **D1** Fork W&B once from the parent at `_step` 390250, the row for the last update before restored step 390251.
- [x] **D2** Publish the W&B comparison report before the first step: [Hero 262K finalists](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Hero-262K-finalists--VmlldzoxODI2NjQ1Nw==), one report for both finalists.
- [ ] **D3** Launch; confirm one coordinator, the restore at step 390251 and the first steps.
- [ ] **D4** Read the gates and post go or no-go to #8506.

### E. Afterwards

- [ ] **E1** Compare the finalists on Paloma, Uncheatable and MRCR at matching steps, using offline evals. Record the winner here, on logbooks #37 and on #8435.
- [ ] **E2** Seal each run. Update the logbook conclusion and the `marin-logbooks` index.

## Stop and recovery

A failed gate stops the finalist. After a fix, relaunch from step-390251 with a new run ID, or from the child's newest complete checkpoint if the fault is an ordinary interruption. Do not fork W&B again for a retry of the same run. There is no parent run to return to, since the 65K run has ended.

issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
issues.body:
Active Iris jobs can keep nodes allocated after their owners stop using them. The controller prunes terminal job records after a retention period (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/pruner.py:51`), but that does not identify old active jobs.

Add a scheduled check that posts old active jobs to Slack for review. One week is a proposed starting threshold, not an agreed maximum lifetime. Evaluate whether Loom should also cancel jobs that remain unclaimed after notification; define exemptions for intentional long-running jobs before enabling cancellation.

Done when:
- A scheduled report identifies active jobs past a configurable age threshold and includes the job, owner, age, and occupied resources.
- The report has a clear Slack destination and avoids repeated notifications for the same unchanged job.
- The issue records a decision on automatic cancellation, including exemptions, warning period, and audit trail if cancellation is adopted.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 Decision on automatic cancellation: do not cancel jobs automatically yet.

The `old-iris-jobs` Loom watch will only report. On weekdays it posts root jobs that have been active for more than 7 days to `#marin-alerts`, once per job. After 4 weeks of reports, decide from them whether to add cancellation.

A read-only count on the `marin` hub on 2026-11-09 found 61 root jobs from 12 owners active for more than 7 days. Many are intentional services (relays, telemetry, `/ops/xprof`, serving probes, dev pods), so cancellation is not safe without exemptions.

If cancellation is adopted, it needs:

- Exemptions: an explicit list of job-ID prefixes (for example `/ops/`) in the watch prompt, and a per-job opt-out by a reply in the thread of the report that lists the job.
- Warning period: 7 days after the first notification.
- Audit trail: a Slack thread reply that names the job and the reason, and the controller's `job_cancelled` audit event.

spillover_issues.author: mcwitt-agent
spillover_issues.body:
The current hero checkpoint (`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, step 393491) multiplies each global-layer query by `(1 + 0.1 · ln(max(n / 65536, 1)))²`, where `n` is the query's 1-based position in its document. `GrugModelConfig.to_hf_config` refuses log scaling, so the checkpoint cannot be exported, uploaded or served in vLLM. SkyRL's Megatron Grug model, which hero RL uses, applies only a fixed per-layer scale. Training in the hero's own JAX trainer, including SFT for #8089, already supports it.

Both consumers ignore unknown config keys, so an export carrying the fields would load without error at the wrong scale past position 65,536. Hero exports therefore move to `grugmoe_artifact_schema_version = 3`, which always carries the three fields (null when log scaling is off). Current vLLM, the TPU lane and SkyRL reject schema 3, and each accepts it only once it applies the factor. Exports already on disk are unaffected.

- [ ] Marin PR: `to_hf_config` writes `log_scaling_n_floor`, `log_scaling_alpha` and `log_scaling_power` (null when off) and schema 3, and `from_hf_config` reads them back. Then export step 393491.
- [ ] vLLM fork PR (marin-community/vllm): accept schema 3 and multiply Q on global layers by the factor at `positions + 1`. No kernel change.
- [ ] Bump both vLLM pins to that fork through refresh-fork: Marin's (`config/external/vllm/gpu.toml`) and SkyRL's (`vendor/skyrl/pyproject.toml`), which rollout workers install. Depends on #10022.
- [ ] vLLM parity: a tiny fp32 model with `n_floor=16` against JAX, with a negative control; then the hero on one document over 131,072 tokens, gated on the bf16 noise measured below 65,536.
- [ ] SkyRL PR: read the fields, accept schema 3, and scale Q per in-document position, including packed batches under context parallelism.
- [ ] SkyRL parity: the hero below 65K against JAX first; then `n_floor=16` unpacked, packed CP1 and packed CP2 against JAX; then NLL on one 100K-token document.

vLLM and SkyRL must apply the same factor, or RL rollouts past 65,536 come from a different model than the one being trained.

Part of #8435. Follows #11056.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
EvalDash pins every scored view to one cohort and defaults it to `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` (#9461, #9752). The runs of the current eval policy (#10197, 2026-10-16) were launched with `experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/launch-campaign.sh` without `--version`, so their records carry `version: null`. The cohort dropdown lists only the verified policies plus non-null labels (`metrics.py`, `versions`), so these runs are reachable only through "Newest per benchmark (all cohorts)", and that mode disables Compare (`/compare` answers 400 "Choose one cohort before comparing models.").

Effects:

- Links shared before the cohort was written into the URL now open on the 09-24 cohort and show no scores. From the identity SFT thread (#10695): https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/compare?models=open-athena-Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1,open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30,open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30 and https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/models/open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30 . Every such link lands on an empty view until the reader picks "all runs" or the unversioned cohort by hand on the model page. Only the `runs?model=` links still work, because the Runs view spans cohorts.
- The default is an old policy. There is no verified cohort for the 2026-10-16 policy, so nothing launched today can land in a verified cohort, and the dashboard asks every visitor to pick a cohort before showing current results.
- Models cannot be compared across cohorts, and unlabeled runs cannot be compared at all.

Reproduce:
