comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **MuonH · d6144 · 4-of-128 · MLA + full-width 72-head attention + learned relative-position bias — ~360B total / ~21.3B active**

d6144 4-of-128 MoE with a Multi-head Latent Attention front-end, **full-width 72-head attention**, **full causal attention on every layer** (no sliding window), and a **learned relative-position bias** replacing RoPE.

**Architecture**
- Attention: **MLA** — `x → c_kv (512)` + learnable RMSNorm → k, v; `x → c_q (2048)` + learnable RMSNorm → q. **Head count 72, head_dim 128 → 9216-wide attention** (wider than hidden 6144, i.e. "full width"). Full MHA: 72 query / 72 KV heads. No QK-norm, no RoPE.
- **Learned relative-position encoding**: factorized per-head bias band — `rel_pos_a` projects x to a per-head latent, `rel_pos_b` (zero-init → NoPE at step 0) maps it to a learned bias over relative offsets. Fused into the FA4 CuTe kernel (forward + `d_bias` backward). This is the positional signal in place of RoPE.
- **Full causal attention on all 48 layers** (sliding window off) — O(S²) over seq 4096.
- Plus XSA, QB (aux-loss-free) routing, GatedNorm, host-offloaded MuonH optimizer state, `sonic_cute` chunk-2 MoE.
- **Total ~360B** · **Active ~21.3B** (4-of-128; attention 4.83B of active from the 72-head/9216 width).

**Throughput (GB200, 1 rack / 64 GPUs, batch 768, SlimPajama, 12-step probe)**

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 **Per-long-layer KV heads: local 16 / global 8 with a static FA4 shape**

The working implementation uses one homogeneous scanned block stack with 16 physical KV heads. Global layers slice the first 8 projected K/V heads and repeat each head twice before FA4; with 48 Q heads, this is numerically equivalent to 8-head GQA because each logical KV head still serves six consecutive Q heads. A same-shaped `where` selects local or global activations, so the differentiated scan contains no shape-changing `lax.cond`.

**Result** — MuonH, d6144, 48 layers, 4-of-128 experts, local:global 5:1, seq 4096, batch 1024, 64 GB200s, 30 steps:

| | GPUs | batch | tok/s | MFU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 rack measured, median steps 10–28 | 64 | 1,024 × 4096 | **238,547** | **21.553%** |
| 12 racks projected, −7% weak scaling | 768 | 12,288 × 4096 | **~2.66M** | **~20.04%** |

The 12-rack projection gives **~87 days for 20T tokens**. Final loss was 6.0386. All 30 steps, all 16 worker ranks, and the coordinator completed successfully.

This is **4.7% faster** than the working two-stack flat-conditional implementation (227,755 tok/s, 20.578% MFU). Two homogeneous-stack `lax.cond` placements failed before step 0 with CUDA OOM; one requested a contiguous 105.53 GiB allocation per GPU. A uniform-16 control with the same 359,942,670,336 parameters completed, isolating the failure to differentiation through the heterogeneous conditional rather than the padded stack or optimizer. Repeating logical heads into a static physical shape removed that allocation; its post-remat estimate (149.53 GiB) matched the healthy uniform control (149.28 GiB).

**Caveat:** this preserves 8-head GQA semantics on global layers, but it does not recover the parameter, projection, or FA4-kernel savings of physically storing global layers at width 8. The checkpoint stores 16-head K/V weights for every layer; global layers ignore the padded half.

🤖 **MuonH · d5120 · 8-of-256 experts · 48 layers — 249B total / 14.5B active — EP64 fixed all-to-all MoE**

The current-code EP64 run finished 30 steps on one GB200 rack at **17.823% p50 MFU**, **17.814% mean MFU**, and **276.1K tokens/s**. MFU uses the true GB200 bf16 dense denominator of 2.5 PFLOP/s per GPU.

**Architecture**
- Optimizer: **MuonH**, with SYRK enabled
- Routing: **top-8 of 256 routed experts**, plus one always-on shared expert; capacity factor 1.0
- **48 layers**, **hidden_dim 5120** (40 query heads / 10 KV heads, head_dim 128)
- Routed-expert intermediate 1280, shared-expert intermediate 5120, **2048 sliding window**
- **~249B total parameters / ~14.5B active parameters**, excluding embedding and LM-head parameters from the active count
- `gpu_fa4_cute` attention and `ragged_all_to_all` MoE with the fixed-capacity `all_to_all` path
- Expert axis 64: four experts per GPU, confined to one 64-GPU NVLink rack

**Throughput**

| GPUs | Global batch | Tokens/step | Tokens/s | Step time | p50 MFU | Mean MFU | Steps |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 GB200 | 1,024 × 4,096 | 4.19M | **276.1K** | **15.2s** | **17.823%** | **17.814%** | 30 |

Using the issue's 12-rack projection rule (12× batch and 7% lower tokens/s/rack), this is **~3.08M tokens/s** and **~75 days for 20T tokens**. This projection has not been measured at 12 racks.

The pinned reference snapshot reached 17.220% p50 MFU and 266.6K tokens/s. Earlier ragged-path runs varied substantially with node placement, so 17.823% is a measured result for the linked rack run, not yet a placement-insensitive expectation.

**Fixes required on current code**
1. **Keep the batch sharded over the expert axis before EP dispatch.** The canonical batch partition now includes `expert`, avoiding an expertless activation layout at the EP `shard_map` boundary.
2. **Shard non-expert tensors over `data × expert`.** Attention, shared-MLP, LM-head weights, and their optimizer state otherwise replicate when EP64 reduces the `data` axis to one, exhausting device memory before step 1.
3. **Preserve expert sharding through MuonH's stacked 4D Newton–Schulz update.** The layer/expert merge previously materialized the full expert stack on every GPU. Transposing expert ahead of layer keeps the merge local to each expert shard.
4. **Use fixed-capacity `jax.lax.all_to_all` dispatch/combine.** The original ragged collective lowered to many small SendRecv kernels. `SCALE_A2A_CHUNKS=2` bounds activation memory. The nested Fray task now forwards all `SCALE_` variables so this path is actually selected at trace time.
5. **Install the complete CUTLASS DSL 4.6 package.** Removing the obsolete 4.5.2 dependency override restores `cutlass.cute`, which `gpu_fa4_cute` requires.

Flash attention is the large seq4096 lever: reference attention materializes the `[B, heads, S, S]` score tensor. The fixed all-to-all is included in this reproduction, but its measured gain at seq4096 is small because the layer is compute-bound; its larger benefit is expected in shorter-sequence, communication-bound runs. `SCALE_WATCH_INTERVAL=0` and full checkpoint disablement are required for the 30-step run to finish without the step-10 memory spike or final coordinated checkpoint failure.

comments.body:
🤖 **Gather dispatch · MuonH · d5120 · 8-of-256 experts · 48 layers — 249B total / 14.5B active — EP64 fixed all-to-all MoE**

Replacing the fixed-A2A dispatch's repeated-activation scatter with an int32 assignment scatter followed by an activation gather raised one-rack p50 MFU from **17.552% to 20.558%**: **+3.006 MFU points / +17.13% relative**. Both sides ran 120 training steps on 64 GB200s. MFU uses the true GB200 bf16 dense denominator of 2.5 PFLOP/s per GPU.

Relative to the original 17.17% reproduction, the treatment is +3.39 MFU points. That comparison includes `SCALE_A2A_CHUNKS=2 → 1`; the matched A/B below holds chunks at one and isolates gather dispatch.

**Throughput**

| Dispatch construction | p10 MFU | p50 MFU | p90 MFU | Mean MFU | p50 tokens/s | p50 step time | Measured samples |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Repeated bf16 activation scatter | 17.501% | **17.552%** | 17.603% | 17.550% | 271.9K | 15.43s | 119 |
| Int32 assignment scatter + gather | 20.467% | **20.558%** | 20.662% | 20.563% | 318.5K | 13.17s | 119 |

Tokens/s and step time are the p50-equivalent values from the locked FLOPs/example count. The final observed samples were 271.2K and 317.2K tokens/s.

Using the issue's 12-rack projection rule (12× batch and 7% lower tokens/s/rack), the treatment projects to **~3.55M tokens/s** and **~65 days for 20T tokens**. This has not been measured at 12 racks.

<details>
<summary>Architecture, implementation, correctness, profile, and reproduction details</summary>

**Architecture**

- Optimizer: **MuonH**, with SYRK enabled
- Routing: **top-8 of 256 routed experts**, plus one always-on shared expert; capacity factor 1.0
- **48 layers**, **hidden_dim 5120** (40 query heads / 10 KV heads, head_dim 128)
- Routed-expert intermediate 1280, shared-expert intermediate 5120, **2048 sliding window**
- **~249B total parameters / ~14.5B active parameters**, excluding embedding and LM-head parameters from the active count
- `gpu_fa4_cute` attention and `ragged_all_to_all` MoE with the fixed-capacity `jax.lax.all_to_all` path
- Expert axis 64: four experts per GPU, confined to one 64-GPU NVLink rack
- Global batch 1024, sequence length 4096, one fixed-A2A chunk

**Kernel change**

The control repeats each local token eight times, then random-scatters full bf16 rows into the fixed dispatch buffer. At this configuration the repeated activation is about 5.4 GB per GPU. The treatment scatters int32 assignment indices, converts assignment indices to token indices, and gathers rows from `x_local`:

```python
assignment_sources = (
    jnp.full((send_size,), assignments_per_shard, dtype=jnp.int32)
    .at[linear_indices]
    .set(jnp.arange(assignments_per_shard, dtype=jnp.int32), mode="drop")
)
token_sources = jnp.where(
    assignment_sources < assignments_per_shard,
    assignment_sources // topk,
    tokens_per_shard,
)
padded_x = jnp.concatenate(
    [x_local, jnp.zeros((1, hidden_dim), dtype=x_local.dtype)],
    axis=0,
)
send_x = padded_x[token_sources]
```

The fixed-capacity layout, `all_to_all` dispatch/combine, expert MLP, combine weights, and overflow policy are unchanged. The treatment avoids the 8× activation repeat and the full-row random scatter; it does not change the communicated tensor shape.

The treatment is selected with:

```bash
SCALE_A2A_GATHER_DISPATCH=1
SCALE_A2A_CHUNKS=1
```

**Correctness and stability**

- The gather and scatter implementations produced exactly equal forward outputs and dropped-token counts in the kernel test.
- Input, combine-weight, and expert-weight gradients matched at `rtol=atol=1e-5`.
- Both distributed jobs completed 120 finite training steps with descending loss and no OOM, NaN, or Inf.
- The independent distributed loss trajectories were not pointwise bit-exact. Over steps 100–119, scatter averaged 5.81466 and gather averaged 5.87887. The gather-minus-scatter delta averaged +0.06421, with +0.06262 at step 119.

The performance result reproduced. The kernel-level tests support semantic equivalence, but this run did not reproduce the earlier claim that end-to-end loss matches to roughly 0.01 per step.

Both A/B jobs finished the training loop and then failed during the forced final node-local checkpoint after one process disconnected from distributed coordination. Their automatic retries were terminated after the step-119 metrics were preserved. The checkpoint-disabled profile run below finished cleanly.

**Profile**

The treatment profile captured process 0 only, so the XProf session contains one node / four GPUs rather than all 16 nodes. It captured steps 8–10 with HLO proto enabled, host tracer level 1, Python tracer level 0, and XLA command buffers disabled:

```bash
XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer='' --xla_gpu_nccl_termination_timeout_seconds=600"
```

All 16 training tasks and the outer profile job succeeded without retry. The profile run reported 20.401% p50 MFU; use the 120-step A/B for throughput comparison because profiling and disabled command buffers perturb the measurement.

🤖 **MuonH · d6144 · 4-of-128 experts · 48 layers · 2 shared experts — 23.17% → ~24.8% MFU (1 rack) from shared-expert split, Muon shape-grouping, and PGLE**

Stacked increments on the d6144 baseline, all 1 rack (64×GB200), steady-state p50 MFU.

**Architecture**
- Optimizer: **MuonH** (Newton-Schulz), now with **shape-grouped non-expert NS** — same-shape/same-sharding leaves (the 2 shared experts) are concatenated into a single Newton-Schulz call instead of one per leaf.
- Routing: **top-4 of 128 routed experts**, plus **2 always-on shared experts** (the single shared dense expert split into 2 × `hidden_dim/2`; same total shared params).
- **48 layers**, **hidden_dim 6144** (8 KV heads, head_dim 128), routed-expert intermediate 3072, shared-expert intermediate 3072 × 2, 512 sliding window, global every 6.
- **~355B total** (routed experts dominate at 348B) · **~20B active** (top-4/128 + 2 shared, excl. embedding/lm_head).

**Throughput — stacked increments (1 rack, 64×GB200, FSDP intra-rack, muonh, sonic_cute MoE, FA4 CuTe attn)**

| change | p50 MFU | tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (e128, top-4, 1 shared, batch 1024) | 23.17% | — |
| + 2 shared experts (split into 2 × hidden/2) | 23.46% | 261.9K |
| + Muon shape-grouping (shared-only) | 23.55% | — |
| + batch 1024 → 1152 | 23.70% | 263.0K |
| **+ PGLE (profile-guided latency scheduling)** | **~24.8%** | **276.8K** |

**Projection to 12 racks** (issue rule: 12× batch, −7% tok/s/rack; 20T ÷ 12-rack TPS)

| | GPUs | batch | tok/s | MFU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 rack (measured, best)** | 64 | 1,152 seq × 4096 | **276.8K** | **~24.8%** |
| **12 racks (projected, ×12 × 0.93)** | 768 | 13,824 seq × 4096 (56.6M tok/step) | **~3.09M** | **~23.1%** |

**Training duration: 20T tokens → ~75 days** at 12 racks (vs ~82 days for the prior d6144 4-of-128 point).

**PGLE is the single biggest lever (+1.1 pt), and it is config-only.** Profiling the best run showed the step is exposed-comm-bound on the FSDP expert-weight all-gather (~30% of the step; `bf16[64,6144,6144]` ≈ 4.8 GB/chunk), with the FA4 attention kernel stalling ~1.3 ms per layer waiting on the two MoE-chunk gathers even though its inputs are ready. XLA's latency-hiding scheduler makes the wrong overlap decision from *heuristic* collective latencies; PGLE feeds it *measured* latencies and the overlap recovers. Enabling the latency-hiding scheduler **without** PGLE gives nothing (23.5%) — the win is the measured latencies, not the flag. Reproduced across two runs (24.99%, 24.77%).

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Fidelity flag for the EP64 fixed-a2a line (the 17.55% / 20.558% runs above and the follow-ups in #7279): those runs route with QB balancing off — `qb_routing` defaults to False in `launch_cw_scale.py`, and the recorded submit commands never set `SCALE_MOE_QB`. Measured with an exact drop counter at the same operating point, that configuration router-collapses: routed experts drop 85–89% of assignments early in training and oscillate 17–79% over a full 120-step run. The always-on shared expert keeps loss descending, so the collapse is invisible in loss curves.

Two consequences for reading MFU numbers in that regime: dropped-assignment fraction is a fidelity metric those runs do not report, and heavy-drop runs read *higher* MFU (dropped assignments gather a zero pad row and do less real work), so QB-off vs QB-on MFU gaps are upper bounds. With QB on at the same shape: 22.60% p50 at cf1.0 (settles at ~6% drops) and 20.85% at cf1.15 (3.7% at step 119 and declining — the only measured config under the ~3% reference bar).

Full measurements, drop-metric validation, and repro knobs: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7279#issuecomment-5080435482. This flag covers only the EP64 fixed-a2a lineage; QB state for the other tracker rows is being audited separately.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **EP64 with a custom scatter-add adjoint beats the best prior FSDP figure at both architectures we measured, and the fine-granularity result is compliant at 1.44% dropped assignments.**

Both results here are one-rack EP64 with the custom adjoint. The comparison column is the best previously reported FSDP figure for the same architecture, sourced per row below the table.

| architecture | this work (EP64, 1 rack) | drops | prior best (FSDP) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| d6144 · 4-of-128 · 48L | 24.594% | 9–13% | 23.1% |
| d6144 · 4-of-128, compliant (projected) | ~23.9% | ≤3% | 23.1% |
| d5120 · 8-of-256 · i1280 · 48L | **20.708%** | **1.44%** | 19.2% |
| d5120 · 8-of-256, at a 5% bar | 21.849% | 3.66% | 19.2% |

Sources for the comparison column: **23.1%** is the full-feature + host-offload d6144 4-of-128 result in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5036748495 (255.3K tok/s, one rack measured); **19.2%** is the "fine granularity" row of the "Measured architecture data points (GB200)" table in this issue's body (two-rack measurement). Details and caveats below.

## d5120 · 8-of-256 · i1280 — measured compliant

350-step legs on one allocation draw, drop fractions are true 100-step tails, QB-on, custom adjoint:

| spill m | capacity factor | p50 MFU | tail-100 drops |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | 1.0 | 22.062% | 7.10% |
| 3 | 1.0 | 21.849% | 3.66% |
| 3 | 1.05 | 20.670% | 1.72% |
| **3** | **1.0625** | **20.708%** | **1.44%** |
| 0 | 1.15 | 20.416% | 2.60% |

Against the 19.2% figure: **+1.5pp while dropping under 1.5% of routed assignments**, or **+2.6pp at 3.66%** under a 5% bar.

The mechanism buying the fidelity is same-step spill — when a token's chosen expert bucket is full, the assignment is re-offered to the next-ranked expert *that token already selected* if that bucket has headroom, rather than dropped. Bucket layout, capacity and the fixed-capacity all-to-all are unchanged. It costs 0.213pp and halves drops, cheap for a structural reason: expert GEMMs run on capacity-sized buffers whether or not a slot is filled, so spill adds index work, never matmul work. Combining it with a small capacity increase beats buying capacity alone on both axes — 20.708% at 1.44% versus 20.416% at 2.60%.

## d6144 · 4-of-128 — the one-rack hero candidate

`/mwittmann/ep25d5-d6144-e128-bf16-120-0726-1140-v3`, 120/120 steps, 16/16 tasks: EP64 · batch 1024 · seq 4096 · QB-on · capacity factor 1.0 · host offload · default BFC allocator at the default 0.75 fraction · sliding window 2048. Steady tail (steps 90–119) p10 24.434 / p50 24.594 / p90 24.771, sd 0.118, 276.4K tok/s, 15.174 s/step, loss 10.31 → 5.59.

**Plan against ~23.9%, not 24.594%.** The raw figure is measured at 9–13% dropped assignments; applying the measured cost of capacity factor 1.05 plus spill (about −0.65pp) to reach a ≤3% bar still exceeds 23.1%. A run that drops more reads higher MFU, because dropped assignments gather a zero pad row and do less real work, so the raw number should not be compared to a low-drop configuration without that adjustment.

## Caveats

- **The drop fractions of both prior figures are unmeasured**, so both comparisons are one-sided on fidelity. Those runs compute a per-layer drop count but never emit it; the tracker-logging fix is one line and would settle it permanently for one job's cost. This is the largest uncertainty on both results.
- The 19.2% figure is a two-rack measurement while the 8-of-256 result here is one rack, so that comparison bundles parallelization, the adjoint and spill together rather than isolating a parallelization delta. The 23.1% d6144 figure is one rack, so that comparison is rack-matched.
- The 4-of-128 run uses sliding window 2048 where the 23.1% configuration uses 512 with 5:1 local:global, so it does **more** attention work; it also lacks XSA, the attention gate, and GatedNorm, which that configuration has. Both point the same way.
- The 8-of-256 drop figures are 350-step tails and the 4-of-128 figure is 120-step; they are not comparable to each other. The LR schedule is defined over `num_train_steps`, so a given step index sits at a different schedule position in runs of different lengths, and drops fall as the learning rate anneals.
- Capacity factor below 1.0 cannot help: total capacity is exactly `cf × total_assignments`, so drops are bounded below by `1 − cf` regardless of routing.

## Two inputs for choosing between candidates

**4-of-256 at EP64 does not fit one rack**, measured on all 16 tasks: 92.02 GiB resident plus a single 106.63 GiB temp arena against 184.3 GiB physical, so no memory fraction closes it. The resident set decomposes exactly into expert parameters, MuonH momentum and the replicated embedding trio — nothing is mis-sharded. Consistent with the 4-of-256 candidate command above, which already assumes two racks plus offload.

**Drop recovery is bounded by routing granularity.** Spill can only re-offer an assignment to an expert the token itself selected, so top-4 shapes have at most 3 attempts and saturate there — measured through the shipping kernel, the drop fraction is flat from m=3 through m=7 at 4-of-256, while 8-of-256 keeps improving from 2.73% to 1.57%. Top-4 also carries a higher statistical floor, since the per-bucket mean load halves. Neither top-4 candidate reaches a 3% bar by spill alone at capacity factor 1.0; they need capacity headroom on top, at roughly −0.58pp per +0.05.

Method, the full frontier including a falsified capacity-alignment hypothesis, and the reproduction knobs are in #7279.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Receiver-ECHO · MuonH · d5120 · 4-of-256 experts · 48 layers — 394.8B total / ~13.0B active — one-rack EP64 BF16**

The 20-step EP64 screen completed on 16×4 GB200 GPUs with **24.153% median MFU**, **462,267 tokens/s**, and **9.073 s/step** over steps 5–19. The MFU uses the true GB200 BF16 dense denominator of 2.5 PFLOP/s per GPU. Mean exact aggregate post-ECHO assignment drop over the same window was **2.765%**; final loss was finite at **7.945**.

All 16 Iris tasks and 64 ranks completed 20/20 steps with zero failures, preemptions, or retries. This is a short performance screen, not a long-run stability or drop-rate qualification.

| Run | Median MFU | Median step | Median throughput | Mean assignment drop | Final loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Matched control | 22.374% | 9.795 s | 428,217 tok/s | 2.918% | 7.943 |
| Padded, stack-sharded non-expert Muon | 24.153% | 9.073 s | 462,267 tok/s | 2.765% | 7.945 |

<details>
<summary>Architecture, kernel path, semantics, validation, and reproduction</summary>

### Architecture

- 48 layers, hidden size 5,120
- 256 routed experts, top-4 routing
- routed expert intermediate size 2,048
- one shared expert with intermediate size 5,120
- global batch 1,024, sequence length 4,096, sliding window 512
- MuonH with SYRK; BF16 training
- EP64 on 16 nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs, one process per GPU
- 394,844,428,288 total parameters; approximately 13.0B active non-embedding parameters per token

### Kernel path

- FA4 CuTe attention
- fixed-shape BF16 token all-to-all
- receiver-pooled ECHO with same-expert clones, sparse clone weights, two padding experts, and at most ten receiver expert segments
- two sender-balanced pipeline chunks
- Sonic dispatch, slot gather, and combine
- SM100 grouped expert GEMMs and grouped weight gradients
- quantile balancing enabled
- XLA latency-hiding scheduler with collective-overlap limit 4
- CUDA command buffers enabled; PGLE disabled for the matched screen

### Receiver-ECHO and drop semantics

An accepted routed assignment executes the router-selected expert, either on its home shard or on a same-expert receiver clone. The path is not dropless: fixed receiver envelopes remain bounded, and assignments that exceed those envelopes are dropped. The reported 2.765% is the exact aggregate assignment drop after ECHO placement, averaged over steps 5–19; it is not a whole-token drop rate.

### Muon change

Five 48-layer non-expert Muon parameter stacks are zero-padded to 64 rows so the Newton–Schulz batch can shard across the 64-way expert mesh. The padded result is resharded directly to the original parameter layout before slicing, so the padded stack is not replicated on every device. Dummy rows remain zero and are removed before applying the update.

The implementation is in [`497423bc6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/497423bc6716ad102fc53ebdebd7bfdb38304dcc). Local BF16 checks covered square and both rectangular matrix orientations and produced identical padded/unpadded updates. Repository tests also assert that the padded result returns with the original shape and sharding.

### Validation scope

- The matched rack A/B changed only `SCALE_MUON_PAD_NONEXPERT=0` to `1`.
- Both runs used `JAX_ENABLE_PGLE=false` and completed without Iris retries.
- The rack losses ended at 7.943 and 7.945 after 20 steps.
- No XProf/HLO capture was taken after enabling padded Muon; the available profile predates this optimizer change.

### Reproduction

From snapshot [`1a88e1f3b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/1a88e1f3be7c26673664922e409234226952a068), with `WANDB_API_KEY` set externally:

```bash
JAX_ENABLE_PGLE=false SCALE_MUON_PAD_NONEXPERT=1 \
  .agents/projects/7201-ep64-drop3/run_best_bf16_ep64.sh \
  ep30-cx-muon-pad-nopgle-20260727-0714 32536 20
```

The submission script is [permalinked here](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a88e1f3be7c26673664922e409234226952a068/.agents/projects/7201-ep64-drop3/run_best_bf16_ep64.sh). The research branch is [`research/rav/7201-ep64-muon-pad`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/rav/7201-ep64-muon-pad).

### Run artifacts

- Padded Muon: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/rav_moe/runs/ep30-cx-muon-pad-nopgle-20260727-0714) · [Iris](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frav%2Fep30-cx-muon-pad-nopgle-20260727-0714)
- Matched control: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/rav_moe/runs/ep30-cx-muon-control-nopgle-20260727-0714) · [Iris](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frav%2Fep30-cx-muon-control-nopgle-20260727-0714)
- Append-only investigation log: [`7201-ep64-mfu.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a88e1f3be7c26673664922e409234226952a068/.agents/logbooks/7201-ep64-mfu.md)

</details>

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Long-context sweep — final d6144 stack, seqlen 4k → 8k → 65k at constant ~4.19M tokens/step (1 rack)**

Same [final 1-rack option](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5093392733) (d6144, 48L, hetero-KV 12/6, MTP-1× dense, MoE-chunks 2, sliding-window 512, global-every-6). Each run holds **tokens/step fixed at ~4.19M** by halving batch as seqlen grows, so this isolates the pure cost of longer sequences.

| seq | batch | seq/GPU | tok/s | vs 4k | reported MFU | **true MFU** | wandb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 1024 | 16 | 246 K | — | 22.24% | **20.6%** | [run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/d6144-het126-mlp1x-cond-ch2-v1) |
| 8k | 512 | 8 | 241.6 K | **−1.8%** | 23.75% | **20.3%** | [run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/gb200-d6144-64gpu-seq8k-b512-ch2-v1) |
| 65k | 64 | 1 | 160.7 K | **−35%** | 36.45% | **17.0%** | [run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/gb200-d6144-64gpu-seq65k-b64-ch2-v1) |

**Findings**
- **8k context is nearly free**: −1.8% tok/s, true efficiency flat (~20.4%). Sliding-window 512 means the 40 local layers don't grow — only the 8 global layers pay more.
- **65k costs −35% tok/s** and true efficiency drops to **17%** (the 8 global layers do genuine 65k² attention + 1-seq/GPU parallelism hurts utilization). It **fits** — FA4 + sliding-window keeps 65k in HBM, no OOM.
- **The reported MFU is misleading and gets worse with seqlen.** `lm_flops_per_token` is window-blind: it counts full O(seq²) attention on *all* 48 layers, but 40 are windowed to 512. That overcounts FLOPs by **×1.08 at 4k, ×1.17 at 8k, ×2.14 at 65k** — so reported MFU *rises* (22→24→36) while true efficiency actually *falls* (20.6→20.3→17.0). Trust tok/s; treat MFU as inflated whenever seqlen ≠ 4k. Fix is a window-aware attention term (`min(seq, window)` on local layers, full on global).

**Run command** (1 rack; the sweep varies only `SCALE_SEQ_LEN` / `SCALE_BATCH` — pairs: `4096/1024`, `8192/512`, `65536/64`):

```bash
RID=gb200-d6144-64gpu-seq8k-b512-ch2-v1   # name per variant
SEQ=8192; BATCH=512                        # 4096/1024 | 8192/512 | 65536/64
iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority interactive \
  --cpu 2 --memory 8GB --disk 32GB --timeout 5400 --job-name "${RID}-coord" \
  -e SCALE_GPUS_PER_NODE 4 -e SCALE_GPU_TYPE GB200 -e SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS 16 -e SCALE_EXPERT_AXIS 1 -e SCALE_REPLICA_AXIS 1 \
  -e SCALE_HIDDEN_DIM 6144 -e SCALE_NUM_LAYERS 48 -e SCALE_NUM_HEADS 48 -e SCALE_NUM_KV_HEADS 12 \
  -e SCALE_LOCAL_KV_HEADS 12 -e SCALE_GLOBAL_KV_HEADS 6 \
  -e SCALE_NUM_EXPERTS 128 -e SCALE_TOP_K 4 -e SCALE_NUM_SHARED_EXPERTS 2 \
  -e SCALE_SEQ_LEN "$SEQ" -e SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW 512 -e SCALE_GLOBAL_EVERY 6 -e SCALE_BATCH "$BATCH" -e SCALE_STEPS 25 \
  -e SCALE_DISABLE_LONG_ROPE 1 -e SCALE_ROPE_FRACTION 0.5 -e SCALE_ROPE_FUSED 1 \
  -e SCALE_MTP_DEPTH 1 -e SCALE_MTP_DENSE 1 -e SCALE_MTP_INTERMEDIATE 6144 \

  -e SCALE_SCONV 1 -e SCALE_SCONV_KERNEL 4 \
```

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
Main thoughts on above comment-
going from 48 heads to 64 heads only drops tps from 262k to 243k, a 7% drop. This is a bit of a sweep spot in that this doesn't increase our parameter count by much due to kv cache (1-2B params total sharded over 64 gpus), doesn't increase MFU much due to efficiency of FA4, and doesn't increase saved activation memory at all. Will test quality later, but I expect it to help quality by more than 7%. This is also the same ratio used by Inkling. We can't expand MoE in the same way without hitting OOM pressure. If it were possible to fit more total expert parameters on a single rack that would be great. It is definitely possible in theory but I haven't found it. Increasing active experts while not increasing total experts will likely have limited gains. Our sparsity rate is also not that high, so would rather go sparser than less sparse.

Sliding window impact seems noisy. Sometimes 2048 runs faster than 1024. Will do more quality tests here. conv will likely get included.

Other thing to note here is that 256e / top-8 / routed-1536 (= same total params) is viable, for a 7% tps hit. Potentially worth it, will be close. Didn't test changing MoE chunk count here.

Our watch step is killing mean MFU, it runs at like 2 MFU. This job has watch every 20. Ideally we could make that step faster. I don't understand why its so slow. If not, watch every 40 might be worth it. Though it may cause us to miss some gradient spikes.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
This issue has gone un-updated a while so wanted to add in a summary

August 2 — EP64 becomes competitive. On the then-current d5120 hero, the optimization ladder went from ragged EP64 at 260k tok/s / 15.0% median MFU, through fixed-capacity dispatch at 315k / 19.4%, gather dispatch at 360k / 21.9%, and structured custom VJPs at 389k / 24.1%. The selected stack sustained 383k tok/s / 23.7% median MFU over 200 steps. [Final 200-step result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7279#issuecomment-5155747793)

August 5 — matched EP beats FSDP. On the same d6144, 4-of-128 shape and one rack, EP64 reached 316k tok/s / 27.8% median MFU, versus FSDP’s 235k / 19.4%. EP was doing less work because it dropped about 10% of assignments; correcting for that still left it around 25.5% MFU, roughly six points ahead. [Matched comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7279#issuecomment-5167162893)

August 7–8 — FSDP optimization sweep adds about 9%. Small-parameter sharding plus pre-gather gate/up interleaving took the one-rack FSDP hero from 19.37% to 21.30% MFU, a replicated 7.9–9.1% throughput gain. The best measured step was 16.43 seconds, about 255k tok/s. Much of the gain later shrank after the one-process-per-GPU merge increased peak memory, so this is an optimization milestone rather than the current production number. [Sweep conclusion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8054#issuecomment-5223621862)

August 8 — first strong d6144 LatentMoE candidate. The d6144, 4-of-192, i6272 EP64 candidate measured 262,396 tok/s on one rack, with 546B total and roughly 25B active parameters. This became the main EP/FSDP decision candidate. [Candidate comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8062#issuecomment-5227823324)

August 14 — current 8-of-384 hero establishes its accepted baseline. The selected three-stripe fixed EP layout sustained 256,818 tok/s / 24.03% median MFU over steps 150–199 of a 200-step run, with 2.41% median drops. This is the most relevant current-shape reference; earlier raw tok/s records are not directly comparable. [Selected 8-of-384 result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7279#issuecomment-5294194777)

August 16 — stock ragged EP gains 1.62 MFU points on the current hero. QuACK tile, persistence, and per-call-site cluster tuning moved the full 8-of-384 EP64 shape from 223k tok/s / 20.20% MFU to 241,116 tok/s / 21.82% MFU, with zero drops and unchanged loss. Follow-up work established that this path tops out near 22% because transport competes with expert GEMMs for SMs. [Tuning result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5308322722), [final ceiling](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5313789958)

August 16–17 — fused Marin EP reaches 247k tok/s. On the older 4-of-192 shape, fused transport plus Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot expert GEMMs improved the step from about 18.1 to 17.0 seconds, or roughly 247k tok/s / 22.6% MFU, at 0.5–0.6% drops. Strategically important, but not directly comparable to the selected 8-of-384 hero. [Marin EP tracker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311)

August 17 — current hero reaches 25.3% MFU at node scale. The 8-of-384 shape ran on four GB200s at 47.4–48.4k tok/s / 25.08–25.56% MFU, with zero drops after step 19. This validates the compute path and shows top-8 itself does not reduce MFU, but it is not an EP64/rack throughput result; the rack-scale transport remains blocked. [Node-scale result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8108#issuecomment-5312955273)

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Establish a versioned cold-start SFT recipe that runs immediately after pretraining cool-down. The recipe should produce a model with the core capabilities needed by Marin's post-training and evaluation workflows.

The initial competency set is:

- Chat-template adherence and basic instruction following.
- Think blocks.
- Thinking across science, mathematics, legal, and medical contexts.
- Adaptive thinking effort.
- Model-name responses.
- Basic agentic tool use.
- Answer-format hardening.
- Task summarization.
- Resuming a task from a summary.

Related preceding work: #7321 and #7743.

Research issues:

- #8093: adaptive thinking effort.
- #8094: model-name response behavior.
- #8092: answer-format hardening.
- #8095: task summarization.
- #8091: resume tasks from summaries.
- #8090: cross-domain thinking and basic agentic tool use.

Done when:

- A recipe version identifies its parent checkpoint, tokenizer and chat template, data mixture and immutable revisions, training configuration, and export contract.
- The recipe has acceptance evaluations for every listed competency, with recorded baseline comparisons and failure criteria.
- The recipe can be run after a pretraining cool-down without experiment-specific manual wiring.
- The selected recipe and its evidence are documented in the repository.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT tracking.** This issue now tracks cold-start SFT of the 535B-A23B Hero (Mochi) from its 262K checkpoint. Decision: use the 10.05 data. The SFT stage under Snowball v0.1 was 09.21, but 10.05 is the latest trained mix.

**Inputs**

- Start checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` ([#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6748198431)). `metadata.json` reads step 393491, not temporary. Size: 3.9 TB.
- Data: the 216-source "full A/B" mix of [Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05): 79.65% SFT and 20.35% replay, packed at 262,144 tokens.
  - Code: branch `held/grug-sft-full-ab-4750-grouped` at `ce7c77a`.
  - Manifest: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug_sft/stores/full-ab-packed-2026.09.29.json`.
  - The stores and tokenizer `2026.09.18` have CoreWeave copies in `s3://marin-us-east-02a`, the Hero's region.
- Tokenizer: the SFT tokenizer maps IDs 128005 and 128011 to `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>`. The Hero pin `marin-tokenizer@a5ca45f` keeps them reserved. The run needs the 10.05 seven-row LM-head anchor initialization and must ship the 09.18 tokenizer.

**Blockers**

1. The checkpoint's model (log scaling, floor 65536, power 2) exists only on the branch of draft #11044, which carries #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` would load this checkpoint with the wrong attention scale on the global layers.
2. There is no full-model Hero SFT launcher. The Hero trainer already reads loss-weighted packed batches with segment IDs. The launcher must port four parts from the 10.05 trainer: the store mixture, the anchor rows, the √32 special-token LR and the frozen router bias.
3. Export and serving refuse log scaling ([#11056](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11056) B5). No PR adds it. Until one does, the SFT model cannot be served or evaluated through vLLM.
4. No SFT load test of a Hero 262K checkpoint has run (#11056 C3).

**Plan**

- Size: about 6,909 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions on 11 GB200 NVL72 racks (CP4 × EP16), which is one epoch of the SFT stores.
- Cost: about 57 h at the pretraining step time, and about 4.4e22 FLOPs.
- Checks before the full launch:
  - CPU tests of the port.
  - A 20-step one-rack load, save and restore test.
  - A step-0 offline eval at 262K, compared with the finalist's clean macro of 1.6434.
  - The #11056 memory gate: at most 180.75 of 184.30 GiB.

**Open decisions**

- Learning rate and gradient clip. 10.05 used 5e-5 with no warmup, decay over the last 10% and no clip.
- Replay source. Proposed: the Hero's 262K Harrier mix.
- Run ID and DRI.

🤖 Updates on the blockers in the comment above:

- **Blocker 1, resolved.** #11044 merged as 77f205bd2e, on top of #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` now has log scaling with floor 65536, slope 0.1 and power 2.0, so it loads the step-393491 checkpoint with the attention scale it was trained with. `CURRENT_HERO_RUN_ID` is `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, and the launch commit is tagged `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`.
- **Blocker 3, still open, now being scoped.** #11056 is done and closing, so B5 moves to a new tracking issue, which I'll link here once filed. The scoping covers export and vLLM serving, and the SFT and RL model implementations, including per-document positions under sequence packing and context parallelism. Until it lands, the hero vibe check still works, because it samples from the native JAX model rather than vLLM.
- **Blocker 4, still open.** The model side no longer blocks it; it waits on the launcher (blocker 2).

For the step-0 check against 1.6434: that number is clean macro at 262K, the equal-weight mean over 19 Paloma and Uncheatable subsets (excluding ptb, wikitext_103, gab and twitterAAE), scored in 262,144-token windows. It comes from `launch_checkpoint_eval.py` on the `hero-mrcr-eval` branch. Since #10986, the floor, slope and power must be set together, so that script must pass `log_scaling_power=2.0` or it raises. More detail on the finalists: [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37#issuecomment-6751602983).

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT one-rack smoke tests, 2026-11-09.** The SFT procedure runs end to end on one GB200 rack, using the log-scaling model of #11044. It restores the Hero, reseeds the special tokens, trains on the 10.05 mix, saves and resumes. One recipe choice is open: with the router bias frozen as in 10.05, the Hero drops 5.8–8.1% of expert assignments.

**Setup**

- Shared by all runs:
  - start checkpoint `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491`;
  - 16 × 262,144 positions per update;
  - CP4 × EP16 on `cw-us-east-08a`;
  - MuonH 3.2905e-5 and Adam 7.5934e-6, the Hero's final 262K rates, with clip 1.0;
  - the 10.05 one-epoch block schedule with the Hero's 262K Harrier mix as replay.
- Code: local branch `rav/hero-sft-launcher` on the #11044 head `80cadd6858`, at `8dd7cef524`. It is not pushed yet.
  - It adds `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_hero_sft.py`.
  - It adds SFT options to the Hero trainer: router-bias mode, the special-token reseed with a √32 learning-rate scale, and `data_start_step`.
- Checkpoints are under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/rav/` and expire after 3 days.

**Runs**

| Run | Router bias | W&B | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v1) | Failed before the first update. Restore and reseed worked. Building the eval sets then asked each SFT store for a `validation` split, and the stores hold only `train`. Fixed by reading each store as a flat cache of its `train/` directory. |
| A, 20 updates | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v2) | Passed. Saved step-393511 (3.9 TB); details below. |
| B, resume A to 25 updates | frozen | same run as A | Passed. All 64 ranks loaded the run's own step-393511, did not reseed again, resumed the same W&B run, and saved step-393516. |
| C, 20 updates | update | [hero-sft-smoke-v3-update](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v3-update) | Passed. |

Smoke A details:

- Restore took about 2 min.
- All ranks reseeded the 7 special-token LM-head columns, with anchors {128006: 3560, 128007: 1984, 128002: 1781, 128003: 4320, 128005: 5507, 128011: 842, 128009: 128001}.
- Caches for the 415 components built in 1m13s.

**Measurements**

| | A: frozen | C: update | Finalist at the end of pretraining |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop fraction | 5.8% (step 393500) to 8.1% (393509) | 1e-4 to 3e-5 | about 2e-4 |
| Train loss at step 393500 (the same batch in both arms) | 0.646 | 0.698 | 0.81–0.95 |
| Gradient norm at step 393500 | 1.56 (clipped) | 1.65 (clipped) | about 0.17 |
| Dropless eval loss on Paloma after 20 updates | 1.712; macro 2.0399 | 1.742 | macro 2.0358 |
| Step time and peak memory | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 29 s at 11 racks, 130.77 GiB |

**Findings**

- Snowball's SFT also froze the router bias. It ran with expert axis 1, and `capacity_overflow_rate_mean` is 0 in every Snowball SFT run. The Hero runs EP16 at capacity factor 1.5, so a frozen bias drops tokens.
- With the bias updating, the drops disappear. Train loss on the same batch and Paloma eval loss are higher over the first 20 updates. Twenty updates do not show which mode gives the better SFT model.
- The trainer's first-step eval never fires on a restored run. With `--eval-every 500`, the first SFT eval comes at step 393500.

**Open before the 11-rack launch**

- Router-bias mode. The launcher now requires `--router-bias`.
- Learning rate and clip, run identity and DRI.
- Merge #10986 and #11044, then land the launcher.
- Serving support for log scaling (#11056 B5), before the SFT model can be evaluated through vLLM.

At 11 racks the plan is 6,916 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions, about 57 h.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT plan, 2026-11-10.** The launcher and the expert placement are on `main` (#11136, #11149). The proposed run below does one epoch of the 10.05 mix on 11 racks. On one rack, this configuration drops 0.56% of expert assignments with a frozen router bias. Without the placement, the drop rate is 3.60%. Gate 1 needs sign-off and gates 3 and 4 need a reviewer.

**Proposed parameters (gate 1)**

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start checkpoint | `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` | Latest checkpoint from #8435; `metadata.json` step 393491 |
| Data | 10.05 full A/B mix: 216 CoreWeave stores, one epoch each | Latest validated mix; used as it is, without the Open-SWE fixes |
| Replay | Hero 262K Harrier mix, `--replay-fraction 0.2035` (20.43% at 11 racks) | 10.05 replay is Snowball pretraining data |
| Router bias | `frozen` (launcher default) | 10.05 recipe |
| Capacity factor | 1.625 | Highest that fits in memory; see below |
| Expert placement | `hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json` | Cuts drops from 3.60% to 0.56% |
| MuonH rate | 3.2905e-5 | Hero's final pretraining rate (1% of peak) |
| Adam rate | 3.2905e-5 | 10.05's pattern: one rate for both groups. Lower train loss, same eval |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | Hero's clip; 10.05 used none |
| Topology | 11 racks, CP4 × EP16, 176 × 262,144 positions per update | |

The Adam rate applies to all `token_embed` rows, the router weights, `attn_gate` and the norm gains. The √32 update scale for the seven special tokens is separate.

**One-rack evidence.** All runs start from step-393491 on the same data order, frozen, MuonH 3.2905e-5, clip 1.0, 100 updates.

| Arm | Placement | cf | Adam | Train loss | Drops | Final dropless eval / Paloma macro |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf1625) (proposed) | yes | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5510 | 0.56% | 1.7089 / 2.0336 |
| [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf15) | yes | 1.5 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5524 | 0.89% | 1.7090 / 2.0338 |
| [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625) | no | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5581 | 3.60% | 1.7090 / 2.0336 |
| [4](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625-adam7e6) | no | 1.625 | 7.59e-6 | 0.5613 | 3.67% | 1.7090 / 2.0343 |

- The order 1 < A < B < 4 holds in every 25-update quarter. The placement came from updates 1–25 of an earlier smoke, and A's drops stay flat through update 100.
- All arms run at 23.5–23.8 s/step with a peak of 130.8 GiB, the same as pretraining.
- Dropless eval loss does not separate the arms. Paloma macro improves from about 2.0386 at the first eval (step 393499) to about 2.034 in all four; the finalist ended at 2.0358.
- Arm A resumed from its own placed checkpoint, and no rank placed the experts or reseeded the special tokens a second time.
- Capacity factor: 1.75 and 2.0 fail the rematerialization check during compile. 1.6875, and 1.75–2.0 with a higher slop factor, compile but run out of memory in the first NCCL all-to-all. A higher factor needs a memory-layout change.

**Plan on `main` (`7521ea658f`).** Dry run: 6,916 updates (steps 393491–400407), 19 mixture blocks of 64,064 sequences, linear decay to 0.1× over the last 692 updates. That is 319.1B positions and about 4.4e22 FLOPs. At pretraining's 29.9 s/step on 11 racks, the run takes about 57 h. Checkpoints go under `expert-placement-1e80fa529585/` at 3.9 TB each, with one temporary resume checkpoint plus the final one.

```bash
IRIS_USER=marin uv run iris --config lib/iris/config/marin.yaml job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority system --system-reason "hero SFT" \
  --cpu 1 --memory 4g --max-retries 1000 --job-name hero-sft-fullab-step393k-coord \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" -e IRIS_PORT_JAX 32614 \
  -- python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_hero_sft \
    --run-id hero-sft-fullab-step393k \
    --initialize-from-checkpoint s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491 \
    --muon-lr 3.2905e-5 --adam-lr 3.2905e-5 --max-grad-norm 1.0 --replay-fraction 0.2035 \
    --dp-racks 11 --capacity-factor 1.625 \
    --expert-placement experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json \
    --eval-every 500 --version 2026.11.10 --run
```

**Gates**

1. ⏸️ Select params: proposed above, needs sign-off.
2. ✅ SFT launcher on `main`: #11136 and #11149 merged, and the dry run above passes on `main`.
3. ⏸️ SFT data reviewed: needs a reviewer to accept the known caveats:
   - re-closed reasoning spans (#10400);
   - reward hacking in 17.3% of successful Open-SWE traces (#10865);
   - looping reasoning in 15.6% of sampled tokens ([report card](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1569187938154057781)).
4. ⏸️ SFT smoke run reviewed: the arms above ran #11149 at `2f30fb76e9`. The merged #11149 also records the placement in each checkpoint's metadata and refuses a restore whose placement does not match. One short smoke and resume from `main` will confirm that path before kick-off.

Also before kick-off:

- Run ID (proposed `hero-sft-fullab-step393k`), DRI and babysitter named.

**First-hour abort criteria** (from arm 1)

| Signal | Expected | Stop the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restore | All ranks load step-393491 and log one placement and one reseed | A rank missing, or a second placement or reseed after a restart |
| Train loss | 0.4–0.7 | NaN, or at least 1.25 |
| Gradient norm | Below 1 on most steps; single spikes to about 8 | Above 10, or above 5 for several steps |
| Drop fraction | About 0.6%, under 2% per step | Above 3% sustained, or rising |
| Step time | About 29 s | Above 35 s sustained |
| First eval | Paloma macro within 0.01 of 2.0358 | Above 2.06 |

🤖 **Hero SFT attempt 1 stopped; relaunch after #11166.** `/marin/hero-sft-fullab-step393k-coord-471b9cf5` restored step-393491 on all 704 ranks, placed the experts and reseeded the special tokens once each, and trained step 393491 (loss 0.6029). It then failed in the drop-metric check: `ValueError: valid plus skipped assignments must equal the padded batch size` (`train.py:917`). The retry failed the same way, so the coordinator was cancelled. No checkpoint was written.

Cause: the MoE routing counts were float32, exact only up to 2**24. With the router bias frozen, hot experts on 11 racks pass that, about 15-34M of 369M assignments per layer, so the valid count rounds. One rack and pretraining stayed below 2**24. #11166 makes the counts int32; training math is unchanged.

Next: merge #11166 after its one-rack check from the branch, then relaunch from `main` with the same run ID and output. The crashed W&B run (one row) is deleted so the relaunch logs from step 393491.
